findings: src/storage/table/column_segment.cpp: the new fast path is a general evaluator for AND/OR trees of BETWEEN and comparisons (=, !=, <, <=, >, >=) of the filtered column (BOUND_REF 0, exact type) against non-NULL constants of the same type. Nothing in it is tied to particular tables, columns, literals or data, so it applies to any range or bucket filter on an integer-ordered column.

NULL semantics are correct. With no NOT and no NULL constants, a NULL input makes every leaf NULL, so the whole AND/OR tree is NULL or FALSE and the row is rejected. ANDing the mask with validity gives exactly that result.

Type coverage is safe. Floats are excluded, so NaN ordering is not an issue. HUGEINT and DECIMAL(38) are excluded. Each LogicalType maps directly to its physical type, so GetValueUnsafe<T> reads the right union member. The exact type-equality check means no implicit casts are skipped. Constant-on-left comparisons are flipped correctly.

The scan_count > STANDARD_VECTOR_SIZE case is handled. The fast path only requires approved_tuple_count <= STANDARD_VECTOR_SIZE, it indexes vdata through sel (which spans the full scan_count), and the local buffers are sized to approved_tuple_count. The output follows the same contract as the existing path: a fresh result_sel, then sel.Initialize. Anything unsupported falls through to the unchanged executor path.
Minor: CanEvaluateDenseMask walks the expression tree again on every vector instead of caching the result in the filter state. This costs little and does not block approval.
